newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo to introduce 18-percent valued-added tax.
newsitem.headline: Congo to introduce 18-percent valued-added tax.

text.p: The central African state of Congo will introduce an 18-percent value-added tax (VAT), state radio reported on Friday
It was not immediately clear when the tax would take effect.
The radio said Congo's senate, the second house of parliament, had followed the national assembly in approving the measure.
Congo will be the third state of the central African CFA franc zone to introduce the tax, which is part of an effort to create a single market of 25 million people in the region.
Cameroon and Gabon have already adopted the tax, which replaces a tax on company turnover.
The other three members of the zone are Chad, Central African Republic, which has been disrupted by three army revolts in less than a year, and Equatorial Guinea.
Members of the zone are French-speaking, except Equatorial Guinea, which is a former Spanish colony.
The zone's central bank is based in Cameroon's capital Yaounde.
